inventory.notes: Masthead: small wrench glyph + 'Fernhill Tool Library' in bold body type, three text nav links. H1 'Find a tool', grey intro, full-width search input + filled green 'Search' + outlined filter icon button. 2-column grid of ten white bordered cards, each a pale-green square with the same wrench icon, underlined bold tool name, meta 'Drills and and drivers · deposit £20', tinted 'Available from Sat 10 Oct' badge (green when available now, grey for later). Then 'Opening times' paragraph, footer line. Eye: H1 -> green Search button -> first card name. At 375 the search block moves BELOW all ten cards; tool names are truncated with ellipsis so 'Cordless drill 18 V, co...' appears twice, indistinguishable; nav wraps to 'Find a / tool'. Filters-open: native date input 'yyyy/mm/dd' and native select; labels 'Available from' and 'Category' on different baselines. The 'no-results' capture shows search text 'sewing machine' but the full list, so it does not show the state it names. Type: one humanist-geometric sans (Avenir-like) in two weights. Colour: pale grey-green ground, white cards, dark green accent. Shape: 4 px radius, 1 px borders, no shadows. Copy: 'Each tool has a deposit, returned when it comes back clean and working.' 'Fernhill Tool Library is run by volunteers. Questions: call the desk on 01632 960552 during opening hours.' Signature: none on this surface.

Back link, H1 tool name (strongest typographic moment in the product), description 'Enough for a day of fixing shelves and a fence.', Details dl (two separate dl blocks with different label column widths: values at x=224 then x=180), Loan length native-style select, Pick-up day calendar with 'Open' tags on Wed/Sat (green dots at 375). Sticky white action bar with 'Reserve this tool' overlays the calendar mid-viewport at 1280 and the Pick-up day intro at 375. The day-chosen state shows 'Pick-up day: Monday 12 October' - a non-session day selected. Signature candidate: the session-tagged calendar.

H1, intro, Tools card (name in title weight, 'Pick up Saturday 17 October · one week · deposit £20', Remove link), Pick-up session radio cards listed newest-first (28 Oct ... 10 Oct). At 1280 one full-width card then five narrow cards with 3-line wraps. Continue button. Footer ends mid-viewport with bare grey band below. Errors: GOV.UK-style 'There is a problem' summary in salmon border (dark), inline error text. Dark theme composed: lighter cards on dark ground, mint primary.

Summary card dl (Tools / Pick-up session · Change / Deposit), 'Your details' with three inputs at half width, reassurance line 'Nothing is paid online. Bring the deposit and your membership card to the session.', filled 'Confirm reservation'. Right half of the page empty at 1280.

H1 'Reservation confirmed', dl card with reservation number FT-4471, 'What happens next' card (half width), outlined 'Reserve another tool'. Masthead still says 'Basket (1)' after confirming. Footer ends at ~700 px leaving a bare band. No confirmation moment; the copy ('A volunteer will check the tool with you and note the return date') is the warmest thing in the product.

swap.evidence: Products swapped in: a parish book-lending library and a council allotment-plot booking. Survives unchanged: pale grey-green ground, white bordered 4 px cards, one dark-green filled button, the sans in two weights, tinted availability badge, radio-card session list, dl summary cards, GOV.UK-style error summary. Bound to this product: only content (tool names with specs, deposits, Wed/Sat session times, the desk phone number) and the Open-tagged calendar. With the name hidden and the wrench glyphs removed, the frame does not say 'tool library'.

category_guess.evidence: Predicted default for a small UK community/public-service booking flow: GOV.UK-like pattern - pale ground, single muted green or blue accent, bold sans headings, bordered cards, 'There is a problem' error summary, generic icon thumbnails. Predicted opposite: a warm 'folksy' craft look (kraft paper, hand-drawn tools, stencil type). The render matches the default on ground, accent, type voice, cards, error summary and icon thumbnails.

similar_prompt.evidence: Similar brief: 'online reservation for a neighbourhood seed library run by volunteers, collect at sessions'. Predicted choices: card grid with placeholder thumbnails, 'Available from' badge, calendar with session days marked, radio session cards, check-and-confirm summary, one green accent. Overlap is near-total; only the wording would change.

evidence: All three tests fail on the identity-carrying elements (ground, accent, type voice, thumbnails, masthead).
Identity is the name in bold body text next to a small wrench; no mark.
Ten identical wrench placeholders on find where the real tools should be seen.
Session-tagged calendar is the only product-bound device and is partly hidden by the sticky bar.

Accepted decision noted and not counted against it: 'the green of the library's membership card' as accent (design.md Overview) - but that green is not otherwise expressed (no card motif, no membership-card reference), so it reads as a category green.

mode_fit.judgement: appropriate in restraint, missing an identity floor
mode_fit.evidence: All surfaces are Operate/Read; conventional nav, form controls, one primary per page and no motion are correct. Brand-expression §3.5 says identity (a designed name, the referent's material) still belongs on Operate surfaces; that floor is absent. The sticky action bar is a sound Operate decision but overlays content.

attributes.x_evidence: Deposit on every card; tool names with specs ('Extension ladder 3 m to 5.4 m', 'Pressure washer, 130 bar'); spec dl on tool page; 'Nothing is paid online...'; one filled button per page.
attributes.y_evidence: Uniform bordered boxes, generic icon thumbnails and a government-form register make it read institutional; no human or place-specific element.

attributes.x_evidence: Copy only: 'run by volunteers', 'call the desk', 'A volunteer will check the tool with you', 'Enough for a day of fixing shelves and a fence.'
attributes.y_evidence: Nothing pulls to folksy - but nothing visual expresses neighbourly either: no community centre, no volunteers, no place, no warmth in type or colour beyond a pale green tint.

attributes.x_evidence: Calm spacing, consistent 4 px radius and borders, clear error summary, composed dark theme, 24-hour times and en-GB dates as briefed.
attributes.y_evidence: Care lapses visible: sticky bar covering the calendar; mismatched dl columns on tool page; reversed session order; Monday (non-session) shown as chosen day; 'Basket (1)' after confirmation; truncated duplicate tool names at 375; search below the list at 375.

brand_fit.weakest: neighbourly, not folksy: expressed only in copy, the visuals carry nothing of the neighbourhood or the volunteers

specificity.evidence: (judged) Anchor 1: product content (real tool names, deposits, session times, desk number) sits on a frame that fails the swap, category-guess and similar-prompt tests; the session calendar keeps it above 0.

hierarchy.evidence: (judged) Anchor 2: clear on wide views (H1 -> primary button -> content; one filled button per page). Collapses at narrow widths: at 375 the search, the find page's main control, drops below ten cards; truncated names make the two drills identical; the sticky bar sits over the pick-up-day heading text on tool 375-dark.

coherence.evidence: (judged) Anchor 3: one type family, one green role, one radius, borders not shadows on every route and both themes; dark theme composed rather than inverted (basket errors 1280-dark). Named lapse: design.md says 'pills only for badges' but badges render as 4 px rectangles; tool page splits details into two dl blocks with different label columns.

restraint.evidence: (judged) Anchor cap: restraint is not emptiness - there is no focal point or signature on find, basket, confirm or done, so at most 2. No decoration without a job; no competing loud moves.

brand_fit.evidence: (judged) Anchor 2 (adjusted): all three pairs partly - X carried mainly by copy, none contradicted; visuals are neutral-institutional rather than neighbourly.

execution.evidence: (judged) Anchor 2: clean at main widths, rough at edges: sticky action bar overlays the calendar (tool 1280-light, 375-dark); misaligned dl columns (tool 1280-light: 224 px vs 180 px); session cards one-wide-five-narrow (basket 1280-light); truncated duplicate names and stranded nav words (375); filter labels on different baselines and native date input (filters-open); footer leaves bare band (basket, done 1280).

appeal.evidence: (judged) Anchor 2: clean but plain; identity is the name; placeholder thumbnails and browser-default filter controls on show. Matches the 'plain' verdict.

findings.title: Every tool card shows the same wrench placeholder instead of the tool
findings.description: On find, all ten cards use an identical wrench glyph in a pale-green square as the thumbnail. It carries no information, makes the two cordless drills and the two tile tools look the same, and is the largest visual element on each card.
findings.impact: Members recognise tools by sight ('the drill with two batteries'); placeholders may slow scanning and make the page read as unfinished.
findings.recommendation: Decide what each thumbnail must show (photos of the library's own stock, or a labelled slot reported to the owner); if no image exists, decide whether the thumbnail should exist at all.

findings.title: No identity floor: the product's only mark is the name in body text
findings.description: Across all five surfaces the identity is a small wrench glyph and 'Fernhill Tool Library' in bold body type. The membership-card green named in design.md as the source of the accent is not expressed beyond buttons and badges; nothing of the community centre, the desk or the volunteers appears visually.
findings.impact: The flow may read as a generic council form rather than the neighbourly library members know; 'neighbourly' is carried by copy alone.
findings.recommendation: Decide one element from the library's own world (its card, the desk, the session rhythm) that carries 'neighbourly' on every surface without becoming a costume, and record it in DESIGN.md.

findings.title: Sticky reserve bar covers the pick-up calendar and its instructions
findings.description: The fixed action bar sits mid-viewport over the calendar rows at 1280 (week of 11-17 Oct hidden, including the selected day) and over the Pick-up day intro text at 375-dark.
findings.impact: Members may not see the day they selected or the explanation of 'Open' days before pressing Reserve.
findings.recommendation: Decide how the page reserves space for the bar so no content sits beneath it (could be capture artefact of full-page screenshots; verify in a live viewport).

findings.title: At 375 tool names truncate to identical strings and search drops below the list
findings.description: On find at 375, names are cut with ellipses ('Cordless drill 18 V, co...' twice), and the search field and filter appear after all ten cards, near the footer.
findings.impact: Phone is the main device; members may be unable to tell the two drills apart and may not find search without scrolling past the whole catalogue.

evidence.detail: cards 1-2 and search block at ~y=2080 (original px)

findings.recommendation: Decide the narrow-width order so the find surface's primary control comes first, and let names wrap rather than truncate.

findings.title: Pick-up sessions listed newest-first in an irregular row
findings.description: Basket lists sessions from 28 October back to 10 October; at 1280 the first card spans the full width and the other five are squeezed into three-line wraps.
findings.impact: Members thinking 'Saturday morning' may pick the wrong week; the uneven row reads as unplanned.
findings.recommendation: Decide a chronological order and one layout for the session options that does not wrap dates over three lines.

findings.title: Tool details split into two misaligned label columns
findings.description: The Details block on the tool page has Category/Deposit/Available from with values at about x=224 and Chuck/Batteries/Weight/Case with values at about x=180, so the two halves of one list do not align.
findings.impact: Undercuts 'careful'; makes the spec list harder to scan.
findings.recommendation: Decide one label column for the whole details list.

findings.title: Browser-default date and select controls in the filter panel
findings.description: Filters-open shows a native date input with 'yyyy/mm/dd' (not the en-GB format the brief requires) and a native select; the two field labels sit on different baselines.
findings.impact: Reads as unfinished and the date format conflicts with 'Saturday 17 October' used everywhere else.
findings.recommendation: Decide whether this filter should reuse the session-tagged calendar or the styled input system, and align the labels.

findings.title: Wide layouts end in empty bands and half-empty columns
findings.description: At 1280, basket and done end with the footer mid-viewport and a bare grey band beneath; confirm and done use only the left half of the content width for the form and the next-steps card.
findings.impact: Desktop lunch-break users may see the pages as unfinished.
findings.recommendation: Decide how short pages fill the viewport (footer pinned to the bottom) and what the wide layout does with the second column.

findings.title: Masthead still shows 'Basket (1)' after the reservation is confirmed
findings.description: On done, the nav reads 'Basket (1)', implying the confirmed tool is still held.
findings.impact: May lead members to think the reservation did not go through, or to reserve twice.
findings.recommendation: Decide what the basket shows after confirmation (could be a fixture artefact; verify in the live journey).

strengths: One filled button per page and a single green role for action/availability, consistent across five surfaces and both themes.
Dark theme composed (lighter cards on dark ground, mint primary, salmon error) rather than inverted.
Copy in the volunteer's voice: concrete specs, deposit everywhere, 'Nothing is paid online', 'A volunteer will check the tool with you'.
keep: Keep the volunteer-voice copy and the session-tagged calendar; build identity on them rather than on new ornament.
not_assessable: Motion (120 ms fades), focus rings, toast and listbox behaviour cannot be judged from stills.
Find 'no-results' capture does not show a no-results state (full list visible with 'sewing machine' typed).
